findings.summary: The 'read sequence once, before choosing the filter' fix has no test anywhere in the ingest module.
findings.failure_scenario: Reverting to two independent sequence.getAndIncrement() calls passes the entire :ingest:test suite with zero failures. Low-risk in practice: SegmentKey renders sequence via %016x, always exactly 16 hex characters for any long, so the desync cannot change the byte-length arithmetic the round-1 fix depends on; the only observable effect is burning one extra sequence number per flush.

findings.summary: SegmentKey.filterBudgetBytes has no standalone unit test; exercised only indirectly through PathologicalKeySizeTest.
findings.failure_scenario: Not a live gap: hardcoding 900 and an off-by-one (+1) were both caught by everyPopulationFromOneToTenThousandIndicesNeverOverflowsTheKeyBudget. A dedicated unit test would localize a future failure faster, but integration coverage is currently adequate.
